Two separate experiments by Wakahara and colleagues (138, 139) lend further support to the concept. In one study (139), 12 weeks of training with the close-grip bench press elicited significantly greater hypertrophy in the midportion of the triceps (corresponding to the medial and lateral heads) compared to the proximal portion (corresponding to the long head of the triceps). In the other study, greater hypertrophy was observed in the proximal portion (long head) compared to the distal and midpoints following 12 weeks of performing the lying triceps extension (138).
